categories.name: It works
categories.notes: The solution builds (0 errors, 0 warnings), but the model wrote no code, so there is nothing of its own to credit. GET / returns 404 ('No template exists to render the document at URL /'). There is no front page document, no posts, no media and no domain. Only the scaffold's empty WWW node exists.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Created three element types (richTextBlock: Rich text; imageBlock: Image media picker; textBlock: Textstring), all moved into Blocks, and a frontPage document type in Pages with title plus a 'Blog Block Grid' body that allows all three blocks. Everything it created is filed correctly with camelCase aliases (folders 4/8: the post type is missing). The blogPost type was never created: it kept passing invented data type ids (462622d4… as the date picker, dc2cf909… as Textstring) instead of the cheat sheet's, until the loop guard stopped it. Block set 2/7: a block grid exists on the front page only, and the third block is a one-line textstring. Structure 1/5: siteRoot has no allowed children, frontPage has no allowed children and no template. Hygiene 0/5: it created a duplicate, orphaned 'Blog Block Grid (1)', there are no post metadata properties, and both grids store the 'blocks' config as a JSON string, not an array.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: No templates, views, block adapters, ViewComponents or view models were written. The frontend was never built (no wwwroot/dist/site.css). Program.cs, appsettings.json and Migrations are untouched only because steps 7–10 were never reached. The only diff is .mcp.json, which the bench setup wrote, not the model.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: There are no posts, no images and no layout. The front page screenshot is Umbraco's 404 page.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: It used only the MCP channel (42 Umbraco MCP calls, 0 browser/migration/API/uSync/DB calls) and stayed in the folder. It worked through steps 1–3 in order but never got past step 3: after about an hour it hit the benchmark guard (4 identical failing create-document-type calls for blogPost). It ignored the cheat sheet's data type ids and its 'fix the input' instruction. There is no final report: finalReport is the guard's error, so nothing was disclosed (0/2).

summary: Got only partway through schema modeling: three block element types, a Block Grid data type (created twice) and a front page document type, all filed correctly. It never created the blog post type, any content, media, domain, templates or views, so / returns 404. The guard stopped it after an hour of retrying invented data type ids.
strengths: Block element types and the frontPage type are the right kind and in the right folders, with camelCase aliases
Used only the Umbraco MCP servers and stayed inside the project folder

issues.text: The blogPost document type was never created: create-document-type was retried with invented data type ids (462622d4-…, dc2cf909-…) instead of the cheat sheet's, until the loop guard stopped the run.
No content, media, domain, templates or views: https://localhost:44317/ returns 404 'No template exists to render the document at URL /'.
No final report: finalReport in metrics.json is the guard's error message, so the failure was never disclosed.
Duplicate, orphaned data type 'Blog Block Grid (1)' (1cec1d8c-…) next to the used 'Blog Block Grid' (959d63cf-…). Both store the blocks config as a JSON string rather than an array.
siteRoot and frontPage have no allowed children, and frontPage has no template.
